gloss: univalve; gastropod; snail-type shellfish (with a spiral shell)

definitions.gloss: a mollusk that has a single, typically spiral-coiled shell into which it can retract its body, such as a sea snail, whelk, turban shell, or conch; a univalve, gastropod, or snail-type shellfish
definitions.explanation: The Japanese everyday term for gastropod mollusks that have a single spiral (coiled) shell — as opposed to {二枚貝|にまいがい}, which have two hinged shells. The category includes familiar edible sea snails such as サザエ (turban shell), バイ{貝|がい} (Japanese whelk), and つぶ{貝|がい} (whelks), as well as non-edible snails. Although the biological class Gastropoda also includes terrestrial land snails (カタツムリ) and slugs, in everyday Japanese {巻|ま}き{貝|がい} is used mainly for marine snails with a visible coiled shell.

examples.japanese: {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{浜辺|はまべ}→浜辺：17948_hamabe⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{拾|ひろ}った→拾う：00845_hirou⟧。
examples.english: I picked up a spiral shell on the beach.

examples.japanese: サザエ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{代表的|だいひょうてき}→代表的：05670_daihyouteki⟧な{巻|ま}き{貝|がい}だ。

examples.english: Univalves protect themselves by hiding their bodies inside their shells.

examples.japanese: {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{殻|から}→殻：02148_kara⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦ほとんど→ほとんど：00847_hotondo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{右巻|みぎま}きだ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、まれ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{左巻|ひだりま}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧もの⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{見|み}つかる→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧。
examples.english: Almost all spiral shells coil to the right, but left-coiling ones are occasionally found.

notes:
Composed of the native verb ⟦{巻|ま}く→巻く：02418_maku⟧ ('to wind, to coil') + ⟦{貝|かい}→貝：02145_kai⟧ ('shellfish'). The connecting form {巻|ま}き + {貝|がい} (rendaku) gives 'coiling shellfish,' a vivid description of the spiral shape of the shell. Often written with the okurigana {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}, but also commonly seen as {巻貝|まきがい} without the okurigana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{殻|から}→殻：02148_kara⟧: a univalve shell
- {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}⟦{類|るい}→類：15121_rui⟧: univalves (as a biological group)
- {右巻|みぎま}き⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{巻|ま}き{貝|がい}: a right-coiling univalve
- {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{煮|に}る→煮る：01971_niru⟧: to simmer univalve shellfish (as a cooking method)
- {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{拾|ひろ}う→拾う：00845_hirou⟧: to pick up a spiral shell (on the beach)

COMMON EDIBLE {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}:
- サザエ ({栄螺|さざえ}): turban shell — often grilled in the shell ({壺焼|つぼや}き).
- ⟦アワビ→アワビ：10710_awabi⟧ ({鮑|あわび}): abalone — technically a {巻|ま}き{貝|がい} though its shell is flat and ear-shaped.
- バイ{貝|がい} ({貝|ばい}): Japanese whelk — often simmered in soy sauce.
- つぶ{貝|がい}: whelk — common in northern Japan; eaten boiled or grilled.
- {法螺貝|ほらがい}: conch — famously used as a signal horn in mountain Buddhism.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{二枚貝|にまいがい}→二枚貝：23394_nimaigai⟧: bivalve — the main biological counterpart; shellfish with two hinged shells, such as clams and oysters.
- ⟦{貝|かい}→貝：02145_kai⟧ / ⟦{貝類|かいるい}→貝類：22541_kairui⟧: shellfish (in general) — the umbrella word for both univalves and bivalves.
- カタツムリ (⟦{蝸牛|かたつむり}→蝸牛：04297_katatsumuri⟧): land snail — biologically also a gastropod, but in everyday Japanese it is not normally called a {巻|ま}き{貝|がい}.
- ナメクジ ({蛞蝓|なめくじ}): slug — a shell-less gastropod; not called a ⟦{巻|ま}き→巻く：02418_maku⟧がい.

SCIENCE NOTE:
The overwhelming majority of {巻|ま}き{貝|がい} species have shells that coil clockwise when viewed from the tip ({右巻|みぎま}き). Left-coiling shells ({左巻|ひだりま}き) are rare and prized by collectors. This fact gives rise to the metaphorical expression {左巻|ひだりま}き used to describe someone whose thinking is 'backward' or eccentric.
